transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place for this. I just... I've been feeling pretty worn out almost every day. 

I mean, it's probably just normal tiredness, you know? I don't want to make a big fuss out of it. But even after I get a really good, full night's sleep, my body and my head are still just... dragging when I have to get up for my cashier shifts. It's not a huge deal or anything, I'm still getting to work fine, but I just thought I should get it checked out... if that makes sense? I hope I'm explaining that right.
How long have you been feeling this way? Has this fatigue been present for more than two weeks?

Well, um... yes, definitely more than two weeks. I hope I didn't wait too long to come in, I just kept thinking it would pass on its own, you know? 

But, um, if I really think about it, it's been going on for about a year and three months? Give or take a little. It kind of started right around the time our older relative moved in with us. And I mean, it's totally fine having them there, I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining about my family or anything! We're happy to help out. It's just... I guess that's around when I started noticing I was dragging a bit more. 

Is that a helpful timeline for you? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Have you noticed feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, most days?

No, no, nothing like that. I mean, I'm definitely not depressed or anything, I promise! I still really like doing my normal stuff, like watching TV or hanging out when I have the energy. I don't feel sad... just tired, I guess. I hope that's okay to say? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm, you know, ungrateful or unhappy with my life. Everything is actually going pretty well, except for the being tired part. Does that make sense?
Do you feel like your sleep is refreshing, or do you often wake up still feeling tired, like you didn't really rest?

Well, um... I guess I wouldn't say it's super refreshing? I mean, I try to get enough hours, I really do. I don't want you to think I'm just staying up late messing around or anything. 

It's just, most nights I get into bed and I'm so tired, but then... I don't know, my brain just kind of turns on. I lie there and start going over all the bills, and my shifts at the store, and just worrying if everyone at the house is doing okay. It's silly, I know I should just turn it off. But even when I finally do fall asleep, I wake up feeling like I never really... settled down? Like my brain was still going. 

I hope that's not too unusual? I know everybody has stress, I'm probably just not managing it as well as I should be. Does that sound like what you were asking about?
Do you usually have trouble falling asleep at night?

Well, um, yeah, I guess it does take me a little while to actually drift off. Like I was saying, my mind just gets kind of stuck on things for a bit. But I really don't want to make it sound worse than it is! I definitely do fall asleep eventually. I'm not just, you know, staring at the ceiling for hours and hours or anything like that. 

It just takes a bit longer to quiet down than it probably should. I'm sure most people take some time to unwind after a long day, right? I just hope I'm not making a big deal out of nothing here.
Do you find yourself feeling unusually sleepy during the day, like you could easily fall asleep while sitting quietly or watching TV?

No, no, I wouldn't say I'm unusually sleepy like that. I mean, sure, sometimes I'll yawn if I've been on my feet at the register all day, but I'm not, like, nodding off in a chair or anything. I can definitely stay awake to watch a show or talk to people. 

I try really hard to push through the tiredness during the day, you know? I don't want to be lazy or let anyone down by napping when there's stuff to do. So, yeah, I'm pretty good at staying awake when I need to be. That's a good thing, right? I hope that answers your question.
Do you often wake up feeling as though you haven't slept at all, even if you were asleep for a decent amount of time?

Well, um, I know I mentioned this a little bit earlier, but yeah, I guess I do sometimes wake up feeling... not quite rested? Like I said, I try to get enough hours in, I really do. But even if I sleep, say, seven or eight hours, I'll wake up and it feels like my brain was just running on a treadmill all night. 

I think it's because, like I was saying, I get into bed and just start worrying about the bills and my shifts and if my family is doing okay. And it's like my mind just never fully powers down, even when I'm asleep. But I don't want to sound like I'm complaining! I know I'm lucky to get any sleep at all, and I'm sure a lot of people feel a little groggy in the mornings. I just hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers here?
